dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a book to purchase. I'm on a budget — ideally something under $15. Also, I'm interested in books that offer advice, you know, like self-help or guidance type of content. Can you tell me what you have in that area?
dialogue.agent:

products.description: Review "Priscilla Long's slim handbook for artists suggests ways to reflect on one's creativity and so become a more effective creator. It is pithier and more intellectually respectful than recent creativity how-tos like Elizabeth Gilbert's Big Magic , and old standards like Julia Cameron's The Artist's Way." --Pamela Hobart Carter, The Seattle Star "One hundred and twelve pages of pure creative gold are here for the taking. No matter the form your creative gifts take, there's something in Minding the Muse that will excite, motivate, clarify, or entertain you." --Krysta Gibson, New Spirit Journal "I found Long's advice, along with the examples she pulls from other books and studies on creativity, to be reliably fresh and unorthodox. I loved being reminded to strictly cordon my messy drafting stage from the critical revising stage and the gutty purveying stage. I liked her form of telling me flatly what to do without pandering to my ego. I admired her various elegant ways of commanding me to embrace the old-fangled: get back to work, and work hard.[....] The simple fact is that I read these two self-help books and I went sweetly adrift in them [....] and when I came out the other side I felt somehow both richly served and pleasantly on my own again." --Bonnie J. Rough for the Seattle Review of Books "This is a relatively small book, fewer than 75 pages, but contains many memorable passages.... In addition to invaluable tips, Long includes helpful questions at the end of each chapter intended to serve as guides for artists to use as they explore their own artistic methods and goals to help you forge new work. On days when the isolation of working in solitude can feel overwhelming, it helps to have the wise and supportive voice of Priscilla Long whispering in your ear that making art is a possibility, and that you, like the many artists quoted in this book, have something to say. Her book will help you say it." --Bruce Black, Wordswimmer Blog "It's as if Priscilla Long has sat down on the couch beside me, offering all she knows garnered from a long life as a working artist. This is the kind of book I want to put into the hands of all my poet friends and students. It's a book I believe I'll be using in my teaching and in my own contemplation about my role as an artist for a long time to come." --The Alchemist's Kitchen "Long has done a terrific job of compiling short chapters, rich with fresh quotes from all sorts of creative people. This small but deeply intelligent book contains some savvy messages you'd do well to heed." --Psychology Today Blog "Priscilla Long has read wide and deep in the practice of artists of all stripes, and she has meditated to good purpose on what she's found. She is particularly good on the cross-fertilization of artistic methods, with the result that this book is wise, practical and illuminating, a friendly aid to creation." --Janet Burroway, author of Losing Tim , A Story Larger Than My Own , Bridge of Sand , Imaginative Writing , and Writing Fiction "On days when the isolation of working in solitude can feel overwhelming, it helps to have the wise and supportive voice of poet, writer, and master teacher Priscilla Long whispering in your ear that making art is a possibility, and that you, like the many artists quoted in this book, have something worthwhile to say." --Bruce Black, author of Writing Yoga "Like mushrooms, facts must be gathered; like dough; a draft must rest in order to rise. Drawing on vivid anecdotes from a range of artists, this book makes her case that creativity thrives in the balance between spontaneity and discipline. Long's voice is conversational and witty, seasoned by her experience as an accomplished poet and essayist. Minding the Muse is a gift to anyone ready to take their craft more seriously." --Sandra Beasley, author of Don't Kill the Birthday Girl: Tales from an Allergic Life and Count the Waves "With stunning freshness and clearmindedness, Priscilla Long explores how to live a life in consonance with one's creative goals. She offers inspiring advice from many high-achieving creative individuals. Readers are certain to come away with renewed confidence and many practical maneuvers they can't wait to try. On the balance scales, in terms of usefulness and of being a joy to read, this short book outweighs dozens of others on the topic." --Susan K. Perry, PhD, author of the bestselling Writing in Flow , "Creating in Flow" blogger at PsychologyToday.com, and author of the novel, Kylie's Heel "Do you get bogged down in creating the works you imagine? Priscilla Long's handbook pulled me right in, to help me move beyond where I get stuck--making space, dealing with feelings, getting out in the world, and more. Her work includes poetry, creative nonfictions, fictions, history, and science. Her other most recent book is Fire and Stone: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? Her book of poems is Crossing Over: Poems . She is also author of The Writer's Portable Mentor: A Guide to Art, Craft, and the Writing Life and the scholarly history book Where the Sun Never Shines: A History of America's Bloody Coal Industry . For more information please visit PriscillaLong.com and PriscillaLong.org.

result.title: Live Like Fiction: 30 Days To Become the Author of Your Own Life Story
result.features: When you imagine the next 10 years of your life, what do you see? If you are drawing a blank, breaking into a sweat, or visualizing a finish line but no course to get there, this is the book for you. Live Like Fiction gives you an original and provocative four-week roadmap to authoring your own life story, and a raft of surprising strategies to make it your reality. Each of the 30 illustrated mini-chapters – one for each day of the month - builds on the one before it, offering relatable stories, cutting-edge research, tested tactics and thought-provoking exercises. Through this bootcamp you will learn the ENGAGE system, a six-step process for discovering what drives you and using it to succeed in your career: E xplore you meaning (Day 1-5), N arrow your goals (Day 6-10), G enerate a plan (Day 11-15), A nticipate roadblocks (Day 16-20), G ain endurance (Day 21-25) and E levate yourself (Day 26-30). Award-winning media strategist Francesco Marconi didn’t just write the book on owning your success and creativity – he’s lived it, as a storyteller, speaker and strategist at the Associated Press and fellow at Columbia Journalism School. Now he layers the tricks of his trade on top of fresh scientific research to offer a compelling step by step approach to chart -- and accelerate -- your path to breakthrough personal fulfillment. Blunt, insightful and practical, this is the playbook for the curious and inspired. It’s a blueprint for leveraging storytelling to write your own narrative and find your path. A must for every ambitious graduate, job seeker, new hire – and anyone with a hunger to become the best version of themselves.

top_reviews.title: Like having a team of experienced mentors in your pocket
top_reviews.text:
After a decade and a half of working with many smart, hard-working college students (including the author of this book), I have seen firsthand how much even the best students need guidance on how to manage their own paths through life. This book does a great job of filling that need.
It provides a quick, detailed course on how to turn hard work into real career success. The progression of specific exercises makes the learning personal and forces a lot of honest reflection.
A lot of career/success books present some superhuman high achiever as the example to copy. This book instead helps readers to create their own vision of what success should look like, and then to attain that.
Honestly, the book is like having a whole team of wise mentors challenging you to focus and think through each component piece of what really matters and how best to get there.

top_reviews.title: Great source of inspiration
top_reviews.text: A very inspiring book specially if you are a young professional and planning your career and life ahead. Loved the illustrations!

top_reviews.title: I cringe at the term "self-help" but this book was the real deal
top_reviews.text: I'm normally averse to books that might fall into the self-help genre, but was referred to this book from a friend I trust, and was blown away. Especially for younger professionals trying to guide their career, the lessons and stories the author lays out are all things you can easily apply to your day to day working life. As our personal and professional lives become more intertwined, it's important to become more serious about constantly improving yourself to succeed in both.

Through this bootcamp you will learn the ENGAGE system, a six-step process for discovering what drives you and using it to succeed in your career: E xplore you meaning (Day 1-5), N arrow your goals (Day 6-10), G enerate a plan (Day 11-15), A nticipate roadblocks (Day 16-20), G ain endurance (Day 21-25) and E levate yourself (Day 26-30). Award-winning media strategist Francesco Marconi didn’t just write the book on owning your success and creativity – he’s lived it, as a storyteller, speaker and strategist at the Associated Press and fellow at Columbia Journalism School. Now he layers the tricks of his trade on top of fresh scientific research to offer a compelling step by step approach to chart -- and accelerate -- your path to breakthrough personal fulfillment. Blunt, insightful and practical, this is the playbook for the curious and inspired. It’s a blueprint for leveraging storytelling to write your own narrative and find your path. A must for every ambitious graduate, job seeker, new hire – and anyone with a hunger to become the best version of themselves.

top_reviews.title: Like having a team of experienced mentors in your pocket
top_reviews.text:
After a decade and a half of working with many smart, hard-working college students (including the author of this book), I have seen firsthand how much even the best students need guidance on how to manage their own paths through life. This book does a great job of filling that need.
It provides a quick, detailed course on how to turn hard work into real career success. The progression of specific exercises makes the learning personal and forces a lot of honest reflection.
A lot of career/success books present some superhuman high achiever as the example to copy. This book instead helps readers to create their own vision of what success should look like, and then to attain that.
Honestly, the book is like having a whole team of wise mentors challenging you to focus and think through each component piece of what really matters and how best to get there.

top_reviews.title: I cringe at the term "self-help" but this book was the real deal
top_reviews.text: I'm normally averse to books that might fall into the self-help genre, but was referred to this book from a friend I trust, and was blown away. Especially for younger professionals trying to guide their career, the lessons and stories the author lays out are all things you can easily apply to your day to day working life. As our personal and professional lives become more intertwined, it's important to become more serious about constantly improving yourself to succeed in both.
